The package drcTMB provides functions to fit dose-response curves using the Template Model Builder (TMB) framework.

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# You can install drcTMB from GitHub by
pak::pak("daniel-gerhard/drcTMB")
```


## The drmTMB function

The main function in the drcTMB package is `drmTMB()`. There is some similarity to the `drm()` function from the drc package, with a simplified input of response and dose variables through a formula interface, and specifying a nonlinear model through the `model` argument. Available models include "logistic", "loglogistic", "weibull1", "weibull2", and "lognormal".

Each of these models has the same parameter names, b1 for the lower and b2 for the upper asymptote, b3 for the steepness, b4 for the location of the inflection point on the dose scale, and b5 for an optional asymmetry parameter. The steepness b3 is positive for an increasing and negative for a decreasing curve. The asymmetry parameter b5 is estimated on a logarithmic scale. The models michaelismenten, asymptoticregression, and exponentialdecay have no steepness parameter; here b1 is the response at dose zero and b2 the asymptote at high doses.
The `start` argument provides starting values for the parameters. The `fix` argument (TRUE/FALSE) allows to fix parameters at these starting values. Parameters that a model does not use, such as b5 for the Weibull models, are fixed automatically.

```{r}
library(drcTMB)
library(drcData)
data(ryegrass)
# Fitting a 3-parameter log-logistic model
mod <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic", 
              start=c(0, 8, -1, 2, 0), fix=c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE))
print(mod)
```

With the `predict()` method, we can visualize the fitted curve, together with 95% confidence intervals for the mean response (`interval = "confidence"`) and prediction intervals for a new observation (`interval = "prediction"`).
```{r}
newdata <- data.frame(conc = exp(seq(-0.5, log(30), length.out = 100)))
ci <- predict(mod, newdata = newdata, interval = "confidence")
pi <- predict(mod, newdata = newdata, interval = "prediction")
head(cbind(newdata, ci))
newdata[c("pred", "clwr", "cupr")] <- ci[c("fit", "lwr", "upr")]
newdata[c("plwr", "pupr")] <- pi[c("lwr", "upr")]
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(ryegrass, aes(x = log(conc), y = rootl)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = newdata, aes(x = log(conc), y = pred, ymin = plwr, ymax = pupr), fill = "blue", alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_ribbon(data = newdata, aes(x = log(conc), y = pred, ymin = clwr, ymax = cupr), fill = "blue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(data = newdata, aes(x = log(conc), y = pred), color = "blue") +
  labs(x = "Log Concentration", y = "Root Length") +
  theme_bw()
```

Bootstrap intervals are available by passing a parametric bootstrap sample of the model from `bootstrap()` through the `boot` argument of `predict()`.

## Effective dose estimation

The `ed()` function can be used to estimate effective doses (e.g., ED50, ED90) from the fitted model, given a specified response level (`respLev`). The effective dose ED p is the dose at which the response has changed by p% of the difference between the asymptote at low doses (the control) and the asymptote at high doses.
```{r}
(effdose <- ed(mod, respLev = c(25, 50, 75)))
```

Simultaneous confidence intervals can be constructed through the package multcomp.
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(multcomp)
linfct <- diag(3)
rownames(linfct) <- c("ED25", "ED50", "ED75")
effdose_glht <- glht(effdose, linfct = linfct)
confint(effdose_glht)
```
